verses.text: Suppose someone is found murdered, lying in a field in the land the LORD your God is giving you to own, and no one knows who killed them.
Your leaders and judges must go out and measure the distance from the body to the nearby towns.
Then the leaders of the town nearest the body must take a young cow that has never been worked and has never worn a yoke.
They must lead her down to a valley with a flowing stream, where the land has never been ploughed or planted. There in the valley they must break the young cow's neck.

The priests, the descendants of Levi, must come forward. The LORD your God has chosen them to serve him and to give blessings in the LORD's name, and they are to decide every quarrel and every case of violence.
Then all the leaders of the town nearest the body must wash their hands over the young cow whose neck was broken in the valley.
They must say, "Our hands did not kill this person, and our eyes did not see it happen.
LORD, forgive your people Israel, whom you have set free. Do not hold your people Israel guilty of killing an innocent person." Then they will be forgiven for the killing.
In this way you will clear yourselves of the guilt of killing an innocent person, because you will have done what is right in the LORD's eyes.
When you go to war against your enemies and the LORD your God hands them over to you and you take prisoners,
you may see among the prisoners a beautiful woman, be attracted to her, and want to marry her.
Bring her home to your house. She must shave her head and cut her nails,

and take off the clothes she was wearing when she was captured. She must live in your house and mourn for her father and mother for a whole month. After that you may go to her and be her husband, and she will be your wife.
If you are no longer pleased with her, let her go wherever she wishes. You must not sell her for money or treat her as a slave, since you have shamed her.
Suppose a man has two wives. He loves one but not the other, and both have given him sons, and the firstborn son belongs to the wife he does not love.
When he gives his property to his sons, he must not give the rights of the firstborn to the son of the wife he loves instead of to the son of the wife he does not love, who is really the firstborn.

He must accept the son of the wife he does not love as the firstborn and give him a double share of everything he owns. That son is the first sign of his father's strength, and the rights of the firstborn belong to him.
Suppose a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who will not obey his father or his mother. Even when they correct him, he will not listen to them.
Then his father and mother must take hold of him and bring him to the leaders at the gate of his town.
They must say to the leaders of the town, "This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious. He will not obey us. He eats too much and gets drunk."
Then all the men of his town must stone him to death. You must get rid of the evil from among you. All Israel will hear about it and be afraid.
If someone has done a crime that deserves death, and they are put to death and their body is hung on a pole,

do not leave the body hanging on the pole overnight. Be sure to bury it that same day, because anyone who is hung on a pole is under God's curse. Do not make unclean the land the LORD your God is giving you as your own.
